issue.title: test_main_prepares_governed_environment walks /proc/self/fd and crashes on macOS
issue.description:
## CI failure

- **Node:** `tests/test_run_pytest_main.py::test_main_prepares_governed_environment_and_descriptors_before_exec`

The helper `_token_descriptors` in `tests/test_run_pytest_main.py` walks `Path("/proc/self/fd")`. That path does not exist on macOS, so the test raises `FileNotFoundError` before `runner.main` can exec. Reproduced twice on this tree (scoped `just check` and an isolated `just test` rerun of the same node). Linux CI would not see this; it is a confirmed Darwin failure, not intermittent.

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: Failed twice on Darwin on this tree (just check scoped lane and isolated just test). _token_descriptors iterates Path("/proc/self/fd"), which does not exist on macOS, so the failure is FileNotFoundError rather than an assertion flake.

evidence.note: Independent reproduction 2026-09-04 while verifying the empty-name identity-facade fix (HEAD 43fe90018 plus unrelated local identity/link-follow work that does not touch this test). tests/dev_update/test_code_swap_guarded_exec.py::test_guarded_exec_reader_lock_does_not_leak_to_inheriting_child walks os.listdir('/proc/self/fd') in its child payload and raises FileNotFoundError on Darwin. Isolated rerun: 1 failed in 2.82s. Same root cause as the named node: tests that assume /proc/self/fd exists.

payload.description: both Darwin exec gaps; this is shebang spaces in #!{sys.executable}, that is tests walking /proc/self/fd
